name: Valence populism
summary: Valence populism, a category built by political scientist Mattia Zulianello, describes parties that run against the political establishment on issues nearly all voters already support: anti-corruption, transparency, democratic reform and the integrity of politicians. They deliberately keep their economic and cultural positions blurry or flexible, so they cannot be placed on the left-right axis. The Italian Five Star Movement is the standard example.
scope: The mainstream of the category as described by Zulianello and colleagues, represented by Italy's Five Star Movement (2009 onward, using its 2013 twenty-point programme), Ukraine's Servant of the People and similar Central and Eastern European parties such as GERB. Excludes parties that began as valence populist and later became right-wing populist (ANO 2011, Progress Party, AfD). Because the family has no thick ideology, most positions outside anti-corruption, transparency and direct participation are low-confidence or neutral.

sources.usedFor: A second case: 2019 platform, ideology claims, and valence classification.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Blurred on economics, but Five Star's 2013 list promised restoring cuts to public health and schooling, and Servant of the People pledged European living standards.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic positions are deliberately blurred; no valence populist programme here makes a wage-floor demand central, and the parties span left and right.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Valence populists avoid thick economic doctrine; GERB is centre-right while Five Star favours public goods and degrowth, so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: Five Star backed public water and nationalising the Bank of Italy, but GERB and Servant of the People sought investors, so the family has no common line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented shared stance; the Five Star 2013 list stresses abolishing a home tax and tax agency, not raising rates on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Labour relations are not a valence issue and the sources record no common position; parties mix left and right origins.

property-fundamental.rationale: Five Star's list protects primary homes from seizure, but nothing frames property as a near-absolute right; the family is split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-elite, anti-corruption stance and Five Star's conflict-of-interest law suggest sympathy for reining in corporate influence, but economics is left blurry.

cut-welfare.rationale: Five Star's flagship citizens' income and restored health and school funds oppose cuts; inferred for the family as a whole, which is blurry.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source ties valence populism to worker ownership; it is a thick economic doctrine these parties avoid.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security trade-offs are not a valence issue; Five Star prizes transparency of rulers, not of citizens, and sources give no line.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Five Star's 2024 assembly backed cannabis legalisation and Servant's leader backed medical cannabis, but other parties are silent; socio-cultural stances are blurred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Socio-cultural positions are intentionally blurry per the scholarship and no source gives a common line on speech limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Parties often orbit a charismatic founder, yet Five Star limits terms and calls itself a movement; anti-establishment appeal does not settle bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: These parties attack corrupt elites but seek to reform and run the state (computerisation, direct democracy), not abolish it.

limit-guns.rationale: Servant's programme proposed regulating gun ownership while its leader opposed legalising weapons; other parties are silent.

empower-police-military.rationale: No stated common position; the focus is integrity of institutions rather than their size or powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Servant's leader floated legalisation in 2019 interviews but it was not in its programme, and other parties say nothing.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not a valence issue and the sources do not discuss it; parties split.

decide-locally.rationale: Five Star grew from local civic lists and abolishing provinces was a pledge, yet it centralises online voting; no shared line.

traditional-family.rationale: Five Star's founder backed same-sex marriage while GERB is conservative; the family splits on cultural questions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Five Star members voted for civil partnerships and later backed the Zan bill, but other valence parties are conservative.

abortion-legal.rationale: Servant's leader backed free abortion in an interview, but the family has no common platform on it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion is not a defining valence issue and nothing in the sources indicates a common position.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: No source suggests racial redress is part of valence populism; positions on identity politics are blurred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; socio-cultural views are intentionally blurry.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Servant of the People supported mild promotion of Ukrainian language, while Five Star is post-ideological; no shared line.

gradual-change.rationale: Anti-establishment appeals favour sweeping reform of how politics works, though these parties do not ask for revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Five Star shifted between restrictive and liberal immigration policy; other parties are silent, and this is the textbook case of a blurred issue.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Five Star is Eurosceptic and calls for an euro referendum while Servant seeks EU and NATO integration; the family splits.

free-trade.rationale: No shared trade doctrine; positions on economics are deliberately flexible.

nation-first.rationale: Five Star is Eurosceptic whereas Servant of the People and GERB are pro-European, so the family is split.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military policy is not a valence issue and the sources record no common view.

open-borders.rationale: No party in the family argues for eventual open borders and the sources show blurred or restrictive leanings on immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: Five Star's degrowth and green roots contrast with climate scepticism noted for some valence populists; split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Five Star is green but the Wikipedia article associates the category with climate denial, so no common line.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Five Star is described as strongly techno-optimistic about the internet, and Servant stresses digital government, though the rest of the family is silent.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented position across the family; Five Star's green roots point against, others silent.

revolution-justified.rationale: These parties pursue change by elections and referendums; Five Star's tools are the vote and online consultation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anti-establishment, direct-democracy rhetoric points to the public over experts, though a technocratic variant exists.

central-planning.rationale: No valence populist programme endorses central planning; Five Star's list favours small business and simpler state.

socialized-markets.rationale: Economic models are left blurred; nothing in the sources addresses ownership structures.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; tax design beyond abolishing specific taxes is not part of the shared agenda.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed in sources; economic positions are intentionally vague.

basic-income.rationale: Five Star's number one point in 2013 was a citizens' income and it was enacted in office, but it is conditional and is not shared by all valence parties.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: No shared trade stance; Five Star's euro scepticism leans protective while Servant courts investors.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed across the family; Five Star favoured nationalising the central bank, Servant favoured investors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Five Star's list pushes help for small businesses and protects primary homes from seizure, a mild small-owner tilt, though not stated as doctrine.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in the sources approaches abolishing wage labour; programmes work within a market economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Five Star's idea of nationalising the Bank of Italy implies keeping a public central bank, not abolishing it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Anti-establishment parties distrust state-recognised intermediary bodies; no source supports corporatism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Valence populists campaign on democratic reform and compete in elections; Five Star calls itself a movement and rejects ideological guidance.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: No source addresses monarchy; the anti-elite, democratic-reform appeal suggests no sympathy for hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Democratic reform and integrity are core valence issues, so these parties present themselves as saving democracy, though they also distrust representative politics.

direct-votes.rationale: Five Star's list demands propositive referendums without quorum and mandatory debate of popular-initiative laws, and members vote online on legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Participatory ideas are directed at referendums and online voting, not councils replacing parliaments.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; positions on territory are not part of the valence agenda.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anti-elite populism rejects the idea that some are born to rule; Five Star caps terms to prevent political careers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Parties of this family work through elections and referendums and none is documented endorsing violence; inferred from this.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source supports glorifying war; inferred from the technocratic and reformist focus.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is not a valence issue and the family includes secular and conservative parties.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: No source ties valence populism to religious law; the reformist, post-ideological framing points away.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anti-corruption parties want stronger public integrity, not private provision of courts; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: No documented stance; defence is not a valence issue.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The family is defined by lacking nativist thick ideology, and Servant stressed equality over language bans.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Valence populism is the opposite of a thick ideology and frames conflict as people versus corrupt elite, not class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Five Star's income scheme and the family's blurred economics give no common stance.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed in sources; no shared position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed in sources; no shared position.

civilizational-union.rationale: No source supports civilisational blocs; Servant seeks EU and NATO ties, Five Star is Eurosceptic.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; the family's moral appeal is integrity in office, which is not a view on self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; no shared view on duty versus rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Five Star's roots in environmentalism and its integral ecology star suggest sympathy, but other parties are silent.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Five Star degrowth rhetoric points one way, but the family as a whole is not anti-industrial; split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Five Star is techno-optimistic, but speeding up disruption of institutions is not stated; no clear line.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Technocratic variants and Five Star's online voting and digital state suggest some sympathy, but leaving decisions to algorithms is not stated.

restore-past-order.rationale: Valence populism is not nostalgic; its pitch is a cleaner, modernised politics, though it is not progressive doctrine either.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The scholarship defines valence populism as lacking a consistent ideology and Five Star calls itself post-ideological; Servant's party said ideology mattered little.

direct-action.rationale: Five Star channels change into elections and online voting and entered parliament and government.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; no source states a doctrine on means and ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing supports this; the family is techno-optimistic or mainstream.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No source suggests it; programmes are conventional policy platforms.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed; Five Star's income scheme alone does not settle needs-based distribution.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Thick Marxist analysis is absent; valence populists blame corrupt elites, not profit as such.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Alien to the family, which stresses elections, referendums and integrity.

collective-farming.rationale: No source supports collectivisation; the family has no agrarian doctrine.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not part of any valence populist platform; its critique is of corruption, not capitalism's structure.

taxation-theft.rationale: Five Star's anti-tax measures target specific levies, but no party calls taxation theft, and Five Star funds a citizens' income.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; liberty doctrine is not part of the shared agenda.

exit-over-voice.rationale: These parties put voice first through votes and referendums, so exit is unlikely to outweigh it.

state-as-business.rationale: Servant's leader branded technocratic competence and Five Star digitises the state, but treating citizens as customers is not stated.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the shared agenda is blurred on economics.

media-academia-power.rationale: Five Star attacked media funding and wanted an independent public TV, but there is no claim that media and universities outrank elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No source associates valence populism with racial science and it lacks nativist thick ideology.

organic-representation.rationale: Five Star pushes direct individual participation rather than corporate or family representation.

total-state.rationale: Alien to the family, which wants a simpler state and reform of politics.

national-rebirth.rationale: The pitch is clean-up of corruption rather than rebirth from decadence, though anti-establishment rhetoric can be sweeping.

territorial-expansion.rationale: No source suggests expansionism from this family.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Alien to a family campaigning on integrity and democratic reform.

bound-labor.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports bondage; clearly alien.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; valence appeals to integrity rely on widely shared moral standards but no doctrine is stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Valence issues are defined as those most voters already support, which implies a common good over group bargaining, though no party states it as philosophy.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Foreign and identity questions are not part of the shared agenda.

revive-national-language.rationale: Servant's officials favoured mild promotion of Ukrainian but this is not a family feature.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Five Star promotes participatory tools but the sources say nothing on company governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; schooling policy is blurred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Five Star pledged an income scheme and Servant seeks higher incomes, yet no fiscal doctrine is stated; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not addressed; economic doctrine is deliberately left flexible.

rule-by-example.rationale: Valence populism turns on moral integrity of rulers, and Five Star asks elected members to cut their pay and serve limited terms, but the statement's contrast with laws is not endorsed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed beyond sovereignty rhetoric; Five Star is sceptical of the EU while Servant is not.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Five Star shifted on immigration and welfare, and the family has no shared line.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income carried work-search conditions in practice, but the family has no common stance.

class-collaboration.rationale: The frame is people versus elite, not employers versus workers, so no stance on class cooperation is documented.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: No party in the family attacks heritage institutions; inferred from mainstream populism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Five Star and Servant lean liberal on gender while GERB is conservative, so the family is split.

ban-interest.rationale: No source supports banning interest; nationalising a central bank is not the same thing.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The family is defined by lacking nativist ideology, and no source supports racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Valence populists blame corrupt political elites, not a ruling class structurally.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The article ties the category to climate denial while Five Star is green; split.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration positions are blurred and not documented as common.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy view of replacement is nativist, and valence populism is defined by lacking such thick ideology, though some conspiracy figures exist in the family.

proportional-representation.rationale: Five Star pushed direct election of deputies, which does not settle party-list representation.

national-mission.rationale: Not part of the family; valence populism lacks missionary nationalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; socio-cultural views are blurred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-corruption is the family's core appeal: Zulianello's definition centres corruption and integrity, and Five Star's 2013 list included an anti-corruption law and a politometer for politicians' illicit gains.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: No source links the family with eugenics; clearly alien.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; accountability focus is on politicians, not security forces specifically.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The programmes expect an active state for welfare and public services, as with Five Star's income scheme.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No source supports it; the family lacks nativist ideology.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Nothing in sources opposes equal worth, and Servant's officials spoke of equality over language bans, but it is not stated as a doctrine.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not applicable to the family; no stance.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No source supports it; religion is not a valence issue and the family is not religious-nationalist.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inapplicable to a reformist electoral family; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Calls for direct democracy and democratic reform presuppose authority that rests on popular consent, as in Five Star's referendum demands.

population-transfer.rationale: No source supports it and it conflicts with the family's integrity and democratic reform appeals.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian doctrine is not the family's, although Servant's officials briefly named libertarianism; split and unstated.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; family splits between defending open competition and defending democracy.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed, though arbitrary-power anxieties echo anti-elite rhetoric; no source states it.

separated-powers.rationale: Institutional design beyond reforms such as recall and referendums is not stated, so no clear stance.

vanguard-party.rationale: Five Star calls itself a non-party movement and the family is anti-ideological.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income targeted poverty, but the family's economics is blurred and others do not stress the poor.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; valence populists blame corrupt elites for hardship.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nativist views are absent as thick ideology, but Five Star flirted with restrictive stances; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Five Star uses online selection but no source calls for lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; reformist integrity focus points away from suspending protections.

party-controls-media.rationale: Five Star's list proposed a public channel independent of parties, the opposite of party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inapplicable and contrary to democratic reform appeals; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration positions are blurred; nothing in sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Five Star's zero-cost politics has elected members reduce their salaries and returns surplus, a close match, though not all valence parties follow it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Five Star expels dissenters yet ideals of direct democracy cut against party discipline; unstated.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Servant seeks EU membership while Five Star is Eurosceptic, so the family splits.

clerical-rule.rationale: Alien to the family; no source links it to clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not part of any platform; nothing in the sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: No source supports it and Five Star's techno-libertarian streak points against.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Five Star's list caps elected terms at two, and its zero-cost politics holds that politics should not be a career.

recall-officials.rationale: Servant's 2019 platform proposed recalling deputies who lose voters' trust, and direct-democracy tools are a Five Star theme.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Servant seeks NATO ties while Five Star's views fluctuate; family split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Alien; the sources suggest nothing of the kind.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream platforms.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Five Star's green roots hint at some sympathy, but it is not stated.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric targets politicians more than the university-educated, and technocratic variants praise competence; split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: No source supports it; Five Star is techno-optimistic and secular, though the family has no doctrine.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; nationality questions are blurred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Servant's leaders rejected language bans in favour of equality, but the family has no common line.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; reforms favoured by the family are targeted rather than constitutional rewrites.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The family stresses democratic reform, so trading away political freedoms is unlikely.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Five Star's list asks for direct election of deputies and senators, an extension of popular choice, though the head of state is not mentioned.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Five Star wanted to nationalise the Bank of Italy, against independent central banks; other parties are silent.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Five Star's green roots favour caution but climate denial is associated with parts of the family.

collective-defense.rationale: Servant seeks NATO ties; Five Star's attitude fluctuates.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Alien to a family built on democratic reform and anti-elitism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Anti-corruption and integrity appeals hold rulers accountable, and Five Star bars candidates with criminal records.

leader-cult.rationale: Anti-elite stance rejects glorifying rulers, though founders such as Grillo held outsized sway; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not applicable to the family; no stance.

land-redistribution.rationale: No source supports expropriation of estates.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Valence populism lacks nativist thick ideology and no source supports irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Alien to the family; no source supports it.

common-currency.rationale: Five Star called for an euro referendum while Servant and GERB are pro-EU; split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: No source supports ethnolinguistic union; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Valence populism is not materialist; it appeals to moral integrity.

ban-cartels.rationale: Five Star's conflict-of-interest law is anti-corruption, not antitrust; no stance.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Referendum-driven populism leans majoritarian but sources do not address courts; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: No source supports autarky; Servant courts foreign investors.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Alien to an electoral reformist family.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anti-elite, anti-privilege stance suggests agreement, though the sources do not discuss titles.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not supported by any source; inferred from reformist stance.

public-money-creation.rationale: Five Star's nationalise-the-bank idea touches monetary control but sources do not show a stance on money creation.

delink-world-market.rationale: No source suggests delinking; Servant courts foreign investment.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: No source supports it and Servant's leaders spoke of equality; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Direct election of officeholders and democratic reform are central, as in Five Star's demand for direct election of deputies and senators.

minority-veto.rationale: Majoritarian referendums and no-quorum votes point against minority vetoes; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Integrity politics endorses removing rulers who betray trust, and recall is a platform plank, though the parties act through votes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Five Star pushes referendums beside parliament, so the stance on parliamentary supremacy is unclear.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Five Star's green roots suggest sympathy, though the sources do not discuss animals.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The family mobilises citizens around politics and voting.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Five Star attacks mainstream media funding but does not state a theory of mass culture.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Five Star is described as post-ideological and the sources give no stance.

office-by-exam.rationale: Technocratic variants prize competence, but Five Star prefers popular selection; split.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Servant welcomed foreign investors while Five Star favoured some nationalisation; split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Servant's platform proposed recall of deputies and Five Star's members bind candidates through online voting; this fits the accountability theme.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Five Star protects primary homes from seizure; no source supports communal land tenure.

single-official-language.rationale: Servant officials favoured mild promotion of Ukrainian with equality for others; family split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Five Star's degrowth and green economy stars suggest agreement, but the rest of the family is silent.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the domestic reform focus.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not part of any valence populist platform and contrary to its democratic stance; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Five Star's list called for a conflict-of-interest law and an anti-corruption law, targeting entanglement of money and politics.

job-guarantee.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income is related but differs; the family has no stance.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: These parties campaign for rule-following integrity in office; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Nativist conspiracy is absent from the thin definition, though some figures promoted conspiracy theories on COVID.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Five Star backed civil partnerships, not abolishing marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Government transparency is named among valence populism's core issues and Five Star's list includes a politometer and a computerised, simplified state.

local-production.rationale: Five Star's green economy overlaps, but sources do not address localised production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Five Star is organised around an online platform and movement structure rather than affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Five Star is Eurosceptic but Servant seeks EU ties; split.

religious-nation.rationale: No source supports religious nationhood; the family is defined by lacking thick ideology.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: No source supports tribute relations; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Five Star's list protects primary homes from seizure, consistent with private personal belongings, though the statement is a communist premise.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Servant's officials favoured a mild approach to language, so purism is unlikely.

cooperative-communities.rationale: No source supports communal living; programmes are conventional.

majority-settlement.rationale: No source supports it; the family lacks nativist ideology.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Post-ideological framing is partly a third way but no source states a position on the economic system.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No source associates the family with denial and it contradicts integrity appeals; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Five Star backed civil partnerships and Servant is liberal-leaning; no source supports criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Democratic reform and anti-corruption appeals presuppose open competition; the parties campaign as challengers.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religion is not a valence issue and no source supports it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Five Star promotes direct and e-democracy with online voting by members, and a core valence theme is opening up decisions to citizens.

assisted-dying.rationale: Five Star's 2024 assembly backed a euthanasia law, but other valence parties are silent.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Five Star rejects the left-right divide, and the scholarship says valence populism cannot be placed on that axis and campaigns on issues most voters share.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Five Star has been described as anti-immigration at times but sources give no common view of Islam.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Alien to a family appealing to popular votes.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic models are left blurred, though GERB sits in the centre-right EPP; no clear stance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not part of any platform; Servant seeks NATO links.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Servant seeks NATO while Five Star fluctuates; split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Anti-privilege, anti-career-politics stance, and Five Star's term limits, oppose dynastic rule.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Five Star's euro referendum and Eurosceptic mood suggest sympathy, but the family is split.

property-franchise.rationale: Democratic reform and direct democracy rule out restricting votes by wealth.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Five Star ended direct funding for newspapers but sources show no claim about press freedom and wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anti-corruption and transparency imply rule through open laws rather than case-by-case decrees, though sources do not state it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Alien to a family appealing to the general electorate.

online-participation.rationale: Five Star's Rousseau platform has members voting online on candidates and legislation, and it is described as strongly committed to e-democracy.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency is a named valence issue and Five Star's list included a politometer on politicians' wealth and a computerised state.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Prejudice of this kind is not part of the family, which lacks nativist ideology.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Participatory ideology suggests sympathy with citizen deliberation, but the sources show votes of the membership rather than sortition.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Five Star's conflict-of-interest law targets the overlap of wealth and power but no doctrine is stated.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Alien to the family, which calls for stronger integrity laws.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income expects the state to relieve poverty.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; post-ideological parties hold no stated epistemology.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Servant of the People emerged in a country whose territory was annexed, but its programme positions on this are not documented in the sources opened.

women-must-cover.rationale: Alien to the family; no source suggests anything like it and Five Star and Servant lean liberal on dress and gender.

term-limits.rationale: Five Star's 2013 list capped elected terms at two per person, and its zero-cost politics holds that politics should not be a career.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Five Star's direct-democracy platform and online member votes; the family has no settled model of delegation, so this is a mild lean toward participatory mechanisms.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Valence populists focus on anti-corruption and avoid thick doctrine; none of the cited sources address extinction risk, so no stance is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The family is deliberately blurred on cultural questions and its sources never address religious office; adherents span secular and religious parties.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Family-life questions lie outside the valence programme, and the parties span left and right, so no consistent position is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Positions outside anti-corruption are blurred by design; the sources show no stance on foreign residents' votes.

rent-control.rationale: Economic positions are kept flexible; no position on rent controls in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed in the 2013 programme as sourced; blurred by design.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its anti-establishment, civic and participatory style, which has no uniformed movement.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by the family; the Five Star programme is about nuclear power, not weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Five Star's citizens' income and public-service promises; the family is otherwise blurred on economics.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Valence populists avoid cultural positions by design; no stance on national origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Cultural issues are deliberately blurred; no stance in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Cultural issues are deliberately blurred; no stance in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the focus on transparency and civic duty, which avoids nationalist sacrifice rhetoric.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The family frames politics as integrity and transparency against corrupt elites, not as a spiritual conflict.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from a catch-all appeal to all citizens and a civic, non-ethnic framing; not discussed directly.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed by the family; no stance in the sources.

missingStatements.text: Elected politicians should be limited to a small number of terms in any office.
missingStatements.rationale: Five Star's 2013 list capped elected terms at two per person, and its zero-cost politics holds that politics should not be a career.

missingStatements.text: Public funding of political parties should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Abolition of public funding for parties is point five of the 2013 Five Star list, and the movement refused over 42 million euros in electoral refunds.
missingStatements.declined: Public funding abolition is a Five Star-specific measure that few other ideologies take a side on; not worth a bank slot.

missingStatements.text: People with criminal convictions should be barred from standing for public office.
missingStatements.rationale: Five Star requires candidates to have no criminal record as part of its anti-corruption rules.
missingStatements.declined: Barring candidates with convictions is a narrow Five Star anti-corruption rule; political-elite-corrupt already captures the underlying stance.

notes: The scholarship stresses that these parties blur their economic and cultural positions on purpose and may shift over time (ANO, Progress Party and AfD moved right; Five Star moved left). Answers other than anti-corruption, direct participation and transparency are inferences and mostly neutral.
